\begin{theorem}[Circuit extension and CNF satisfiability]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.toCNF_extension_iff}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.toCNF_extension_iff}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval_tseitinGates_values, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toCNF, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.values, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.values_getD_eq_of_eval_tseitinGates, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.values_getD_input}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits, with each gate reading at most two
vertices, and let $\sigma:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$ be an assignment. There exists an
assignment $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$ agreeing with $\sigma$ on every index below $n$
and satisfying the CNF encoding of $C$ if and only if $C$ evaluates to true on the first
$n$ bits specified by $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Flat-map length bound]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.length_le_length_flatMap}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.length_le_length_flatMap}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ map elements of a type $\alpha$ to finite lists over a type $\beta$, let
$a\in\alpha$, and let $l$ be a finite list of elements of $\alpha$. If $a$ occurs in
$l$, then the length of $f(a)$ is at most the length of the list obtained by
concatenating $f(x)$ over all entries $x$ of $l$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on a folded maximum]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.foldr_max_le}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.foldr_max_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ be a finite list of natural numbers and let $B\in\mathbb{N}$. If every entry of
$L$ is at most $B$, then folding the maximum operation over $L$, starting from $0$,
gives a value at most $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variable count bounded by encoding length]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.numVars_le_length_serialize}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.numVars_le_length_serialize}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.foldr_max_le, Complexity.TQBFHard.length_le_length_flatMap, Std.Sat.CNF.numVars, Std.Sat.CNF.serialize, Std.Sat.CNF.serializeClause, Std.Sat.CNF.serializeLit}
\difficulty{5}
For every CNF formula $\varphi$ whose variables are indexed by natural numbers, its
variable count is at most the length of its binary encoding.
\end{theorem}
